### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **57** documentable anchor(s).

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f78bd2362da8903b27ee8f09c04776c7d15170a2` — the merge of head `06a3c7640b5de8e8d3c0d665d426137e8d42077b` into base `93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f78bd2362da8903b27ee8f09c04776c7d15170a2 && git checkout f78bd2362da8903b27ee8f09c04776c7d15170a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f 06a3c7640b5de8e8d3c0d665d426137e8d42077b && git checkout -B drift-repro 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f && git merge --no-ff 06a3c7640b5de8e8d3c0d665d426137e8d42077b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head dc763477 · 2026-11-25T03:11Z

L1: REWORK (L1-w, zone wf-A)
Head-sha: `dc763477535b0b6aa3397c14bc827154979afcc9`

There is no must-fix. Two should-fix findings are open, so under the merge standard this head is REWORK. No L2 is owed: nothing under `packages/spec/src/**` moves, the declaration is `Clause-②: no`, there is no narrowing arm, and `approval` was already a `FeedItemType`. This is **Tier S**: no governed path, and 1,072 changed lines on this card's only PR. wf-A lands it after ACCEPT.

### Should-fix

- **S1. Every reader sees the approval line in English, whatever their language.** The producer stores `summary` as fixed English text: `Submitted for approval`, `Approved · <step>`, `Rejected · <step>` and `Recalled the approval request` (`APPROVAL_ACTIVITY_STEPS`). The console draws that text as it is: `renderApprovalLine` shows `item.body`, which is `row.summary` (`activityRowToFeedItem`).
  - Nothing translates it on read. plugin-audit re-composes a summary in the reader's language only for a row that carries an `ActivitySummaryMessage` code (`activity-summary-message.ts`, #26167), and these rows carry none.
  - The step label is frozen too. It is the request's `current_step_label` as stored, whereas the approvals door localizes labels per reader (`reader-locale-labels`).
  - Example: a zh-CN reader's 动态 shows `Approved · 经理审批` between CRUD rows written in Chinese. This is the defect #26167 fixed for the CRUD mirror ("a zh-CN reader saw `Created Contract "…"` forever").
  - Fix, either way: (a) the console composes the line from `metadata.action`, plus `metadata.step_label` where the row has one, through i18n keys in every locale pack, and keeps `summary` as the fallback for an unknown action; or (b) plugin-approvals re-composes `summary` on read in the reader's locale, the same sequence its `reader-locale-labels` uses. Pin a non-English reader either way.
- **S2. The claim's file surface was not amended for the files outside it.** Claim 7147655087 names `plugin-approvals/src/**`, `plugin-detail/src/renderers/**`, `app-shell/**` and the changesets. The diff also moves these files:
  - `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/RecordChatterPanel.tsx`
  - `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx`
  - `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/recordTimelineStream.ts`
  - `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx`
  - the tenant-audit write census `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts/plugins/plugin-approvals.md`

  The PR body already describes each of them. The zone amends the claim in the same round. This is the same gap as L1 S1 on #37179.

### Nits (fix any that ride the same push; each one left needs a follow-up card under the nit rule)

- **N1.** `revise` (sent back for changes), `resubmit` and `cancel` write no entry. A record sent back and then resubmitted shows `Approved · Step 1` and then nothing, while the request is pending again. The card's four kinds are delivered, so `Fixes` holds. The rest is a follow-up card.
- **N2.** The producer writes for an object with `enable.activities: false`, whose timeline is hidden (`object.zod.ts`: "explicit false stops mirroring and hides the timeline"). Those rows are never read. Either honor the flag, or say in the module header why the flag does not apply.
- **N3.** The integration test pins the approved entry only as `/^Approved/`. The `· <step>` half, which the changeset names, is unpinned.
- **N4.** The PR body's 维护者速读 says 「撤回本 PR 即恢复原样」. Rows already written stay in `sys_activity` for up to 14 days after a revert. Without this PR's read gate, they are served to every record reader, and they draw as generic system lines. The sentence should say so.

### Read and found right (head dc763477)

- `l1-face --pr 37188`: 13 items clean. Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #35723` binds only this card. The declarations are `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset names plugin-approvals and plugin-detail, both published, and app-shell, which is private and harmless. `patch` is right for kind `none`. Floors and all checks are green: 58 success, 9 expected skips, 0 failed. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **`Fixes` is right, once the findings close.** Every Done-when line is in the tree:
  - one entry per submitted / approved / rejected / recalled step;
  - the one-line row from #35708;
  - 「看审批」 opens the 审批 tab through `RecordViewApprovalsContext`;
  - `approval` is in `PRODUCED_FEED_TYPES`;
  - a real-kernel test shows one entry per step, none for a reader with no approval access, and served under the record-reader opt-in.
- **Producer.** It is an `afterInsert` on `sys_approval_action`.
  - `actionRow` is called with the pre-decision request, because the decision is audited before the tally, so `step_label` is the step decided.
  - The hook is code-registered (no `meta`), so it opens no after-abort unit (`opensAfterAbortUnit`: "Code-registered hooks (no `meta`) open no unit"). `approval-service.ts` threads no transaction, so a failed append is caught and cannot roll the decision log back.
  - It writes nothing without plugin-audit (the `has(ACTIVITY_OBJECT, 'type')` probe). The tenant is threaded and the census was regenerated. Both new `actor_id` reads are classified `display`.
- **Read gate.** It adds a conjunct on `find` / `findOne` / `count` / `aggregate`, so the record page's count and rows agree.
  - Rows with a null or other `source_object` pass, and approval rows are kept by `source_id ∈ visibleRequestIdsFor(context, target)`. That is the same source and the same unbounded-`$in` pattern as the request-table gate.
  - A read with `object_name` and `record_id` pinned asks with the record, so `approvalsVisibleToReaders` serves readers.
  - It fails closed for approval rows only. It is bound beside the producer inside the middleware branch, so no entry is written where reads cannot be narrowed.
- **Console.** It reads the full triple (`system` + `metadata.kind: 'approval'` + `sys_approval_request`). `system` is platform-only, so an app's own row cannot draw as an approval. `viewApprovals` is `null` when the reader is served no requests. `openRecordApprovals` is a plain function below the early returns (no hook-order change), and the tag and the stream share it. The ablation reported in the body turns the harness pin red.
- **Changeset and `plugin-detail.mdx`, sentence by sentence.**
  - The four kinds, "no decision comment", the ADR-0052 §5 shape, the no-plugin-audit case, "logged once at `error`", the visibility tiers, count/rows agreement, the triple, `APPROVAL_ACTIVITY_FEED_TYPE` and the 14-day reap all hold. The reap is `retention: { maxAge: '14d' }` in `sys-activity.object.ts`.
  - In the docs: "six produced", the seven unproduced kinds listed (13 − 6) and `types: ['call']` as the unproduced example all hold.
  - After S1, the changeset's `Approved · <step>` wording needs one more read against the fix.

### Path to ACCEPT

1. Card thread: one push for S1 with its pin, plus any nits it takes.
2. Zone: amend the claim (S2), and file a card for each nit left.
3. L1-w: I read the delta on that head.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head 06a3c764 · 2026-11-25T05:24Z

Head-sha: `06a3c7640b5de8e8d3c0d665d426137e8d42077b`

No must-fix, no should-fix. No L2 is owed: nothing under `packages/spec/src/**` moves, `Clause-②: no`, and no narrowing arm. Tier S: no governed path; the PR's own net diff is 19 files, +1409/−52, on this card's only PR. wf-A lands it after green.

### Round 1 (7151680146), closed

- **S1 closed (route b, the #26167 shape).** The stored `summary` is the English sentence from plugin-approvals' own catalog (`approvalActivity*`, `translations/messages.ts`, in all eleven packs), composed through `approvalActivityMessage` + `interpolate(enMessages…)`.
  - The row now also carries `flow_name` / `step_name` in `metadata`.
  - `bindApprovalActivityLocale` (a `sys_activity` middleware on `find` / `findOne`, non-system reads with a locale only) re-composes the line through `readerLabelsFor`, the approvals door's own lookup. The step label comes from `flows.<flow>.approvals.<node>.label`, else the stored label.
  - It recognises an entry by the full triple. A read projecting `summary` alone borrows `type` / `source_object` / `metadata` and strips them again before the rows return.
  - A missing key, no locale, no `i18n` service or a throw all leave the stored line.
  - The pins cover a zh-CN reader (`已批准 · 经理审批`, with an app-pack step label), a summary-only projection, a reader with no locale and a system read. The reported ablation turns the zh-CN pin red.
- **S2 closed.** The claim is amended; the latest amendment, 7153690278, also adds `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`. Row 17 of that census now names `bindApprovalActivityLocale` and the `isSystem` read that skips it, and the per-file count row is added.
- **N1 closed.** `revise`, `resubmit` and `cancel` write entries (`APPROVAL_ACTIVITY_STEPS`), each pinned. `cancel` is written only when the governed record is deleted (`approval-service.ts`, the deleted-record path), which matches the changeset's "cancelled (the record was deleted)".
- **N2 closed.** `objectMutesActivities` honours `enable.activities: false` at write, as `audit-writers.ts` does.
- **N3 closed.** The approved and rejected lines are pinned exactly.
- **N4 closed.** The 维护者速读 now says rows already written stay up to 14 days after a revert and are then served to every record reader as generic system lines.

### Read and found right (head 06a3c764)

- `l1-face --pr 37188`: 13 items clean. 60 success, 11 expected skips, 0 failed, 0 pending. `mergeable_state` was not yet computed at my read; wf-A reports it clean. The head carries a merge of `main`.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence,** against `approval-activity-feed.ts` at this head:
  - the seven kinds and their lines;
  - the `enable.activities: false` sentence;
  - the metadata it carries;
  - "the stored `summary` is the English line from plugin-approvals' own catalog";
  - the reader-locale re-composition and its step-label source;
  - "A system read, or a read with no locale, gets the stored English line";
  - the unchanged failed-append sentence.

  The `system-context.mdx` row reads the same as the middleware's `context.isSystem` skip.
- Round 1's reads still stand on the parts that did not move: the producer, the read gate, the console mapping and the `RecordViewApprovalsContext` wiring.

### Landing to-do

`Fixes #35723` closes the card on merge.
